evidence.claim: CLI has four distinct turn-driving code paths (ACP, interactive legacy useGeminiStream, interactive agent-session useAgentStream, non-interactive legacy, non-interactive agent-session).
Interactive continuation is a recursive React callback: handleCompletedTools calls submitQuery(responseParts, { isContinuation: true }, prompt_ids[0]).
Non-interactive legacy drives continuation with an imperative while(true) loop; currentMessages is rewritten with tool response parts each turn.
OutputFormat.{TEXT,JSON,STREAM_JSON} selects three disjoint emission paths in non-interactive mode.
ACP bypasses Turn and GeminiClient.sendMessageStream; GeminiAgent.prompt calls chat.sendMessageStream directly and owns its own tool-call continuation loop.
Non-interactive slash-command loaders omit SkillCommandLoader; interactive includes it.
ACP maintains a third, independent slash-command registry with Memory/Extensions/Init/Restore/About/Help commands; it does not use CommandService or SlashCommandResolver.

Interactive cancellation is escape-key driven via useKeypress -> cancelOngoingRequest; non-interactive cancellation uses readline Ctrl+C detection with abortController.abort(); agent-session additionally calls session.abort() and rethrows FatalCancellationError.
No /pollux slash command or any pollux-related code exists in packages/cli/src (rg -i pollux -> 0 matches).
evidence.notes: VT-9 negative claim; search command: rg -i "pollux" packages/cli/src -> 0 matches.

evidence.claim: handleFinalSubmit arbitrates four branches: safe-concurrent slash during responding, model-steering hint injection, normal submitQuery with permissions check, and queued message while initializing.
useAgentStream has explicit parity TODOs for loop-detection confirmation, shell focus / background tasks, and plan-mode approval transitions.
Non-interactive agent-session reconstructs Fatal* error instances from AgentEvent._meta.errorName because typed error identity is lost across the protocol boundary.

SlashCommandResolver rules: skill+extensionName always prefixed; incoming BUILT_IN keeps name and displaces; non-built-in conflicts use source-derived prefix with ':' for skill/extension-file and '.' for user/workspace/MCP; numeric suffixes appended on re-collision.

contradictions.description: POLLUX_SPEC.md claim 'packages/cli unchanged' contradicts Phase 7 (/pollux) and Risk 1 (stream hook crash). No /pollux code exists yet, but the spec requires it.

Spec §3/§7 assume a single interceptor between GeminiClient and Turn, but CLI has four drivers hitting three different core entrypoints (GeminiChat via ACP, LegacyAgentSession via agent-session modes, GeminiClient via legacy modes).
Non-interactive slash-command loaders silently drop SkillCommandLoader, so skill-provided commands are only available in interactive mode.
ACP handleCommand accepts and ignores a parts: Part[] argument (eslint-disable no-unused-vars), so non-text prompt parts can never influence command behavior.
AppContainer.tsx conditionally calls useGeminiStream vs useAgentStream behind eslint-disable rules-of-hooks. Runtime toggle of getAgentSessionInteractiveEnabled() would corrupt hook state.

risks.description: A Pollux interceptor placed only between GeminiClient and Turn will silently miss the ACP and agent-session drivers; benchmarks under those modes over-estimate Pollux's value-add.
risks.suggestedGuard: Tag every turn start with a driver identifier (interactive-legacy / interactive-agent / non-interactive-legacy / non-interactive-agent / acp) and require Pollux to emit one log per driver; missing tag = un-intercepted path.

risks.description: processGeminiStreamEvents has an exhaustive switch over ServerGeminiEventType; adding any new event type without updating it crashes the interactive shell (Risk 1 stream splice corruption).
risks.suggestedGuard: When introducing Pollux events, update both useGeminiStream processGeminiStreamEvents and nonInteractiveCli.ts non-interactive switch together.

risks.description: AppContainer's conditional hook call (useAgentStream vs useGeminiStream) breaks if the flag toggles at runtime.
risks.suggestedGuard: Treat getAgentSessionInteractiveEnabled() as mount-time-only; assert-and-fail on mid-session flag change.

risks.description: handleCompletedTools continues with prompt_ids[0] unilaterally; telemetry mis-attributes continuation turns when a batch spans multiple prompts.
risks.suggestedGuard: Assert all prompt_ids are equal or split the continuation per prompt_id.

risks.description: ACP handleCommand reads commandText from the first contiguous text parts only; binary-prefixed prompts skip command interception silently.
risks.suggestedGuard: Scan all text parts or reject non-text-first prompts when starting with '/' or '$' is plausible.

risks.description: gemini.tsx creates sessionId before config.initialize() in non-interactive mode; a later init that mutates the id would cause stale session ids in JSON output.
risks.suggestedGuard: Freeze the session id at construction; forbid mutation in initialize().

openQuestions: Is the absence of SkillCommandLoader in non-interactive mode intentional, or a regression?
Can config.getAgentSessionInteractiveEnabled() change mid-session via settings hot reload?
Should ACP's handleCommand support multimodal-prefixed command prompts?
Which of the four turn drivers should Pollux instrument first, and how is benchmark fairness preserved when drivers use different router integration points?
Should handleCompletedTools preserve per-tool prompt_id instead of collapsing to prompt_ids[0]?
Should the /pollux slash command live in BuiltinCommandLoader or a dedicated extension (and what about ACP and non-interactive parity)?
